learningObjective: Compare the per-rank bandwidth costs of ring-AllGather, ring-ReduceScatter and ring-AllReduce and the relationships between them.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a payload of S bytes on N ranks with a ring topology, the per-rank bandwidth cost of AllGather is (N-1)/N · S; the per-rank bandwidth cost of ReduceScatter is also (N-1)/N · S; and AllReduce equals ReduceScatter followed by AllGather, giving 2·(N-1)/N · S.
nonImplications: Does not imply that on non-ring topologies (tree, hypercube) the same equalities hold.
Does not imply that AllGather = ReduceScatter semantically; they only match in bandwidth cost on a ring.

sourceMappings.locator: Ch. 6 cost analysis of ring-based collectives

canonicalClaims.claim: For AllGather starting from a per-rank shard of size S/N, the per-rank input is S/N but each rank must end with the full S bytes; it therefore receives (N-1)·(S/N) = (N-1)/N · S bytes.
conditions: Starting shard size is S/N per rank (total payload is S).
nonImplications: Does not imply that each rank sends (N-1)·(S/N) bytes in a single message; the ring transports these through N-1 hops of S/N each.

misconceptions.claim: AllGather on a ring costs S per rank because each rank ends with the full tensor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Each rank already contributes S/N; it only receives the remaining (N-1)/N · S from peers.

misconceptions.claim: ReduceScatter costs 2·(N-1)/N · S per rank because each rank sends its input and then receives a reduced shard.
misconceptions.whyWrong: ReduceScatter on a ring pipelines the reduction so each rank sends (N-1) chunks of size S/N total, giving (N-1)/N · S — the same as AllGather, not double.

misconceptions.claim: AllReduce cannot be decomposed into ReduceScatter and AllGather because the two collectives have incompatible axes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: This decomposition is the standard implementation and the reason ring-AllReduce cost is 2·(N-1)/N · S.
